summary.headline: Cera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.5% (volume-led) to INR 486 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.1% on one-time factors management says reverse from Q3.
summary.overview:
Revenue from operations grew about 19.5% YoY to INR 486 crore, with Sanitaryware up 14%, Faucetware up 25% and growth mainly volume-driven. EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 49.2 crore (10.1% margin vs 13.1% a year ago), which management attributed to a wage settlement, under-absorption from single-kiln operation in April-May, project-order foreclosures and delayed price pass-through. PAT was INR 45 crore vs INR 47 crore. Turnover discounts were reclassified from expenses into revenue deductions, lowering reported revenue by about 2.5-3% with no absolute profit impact. FY27 guidance of 18-20% revenue growth and 13.5-14% EBITDA margin was maintained.</overview>

segments.name: Sanitaryware
segments.commentary: 47% of revenue; grew 14% YoY (volume ~10%, price ~2%, mix ~2%). Capacity utilisation 61% in Q1, roughly 80% across both plants from June.

segments.name: Faucetware
segments.commentary: 40% of revenue; grew 25% YoY (volume 18%, price 4%, mix 3%). Utilisation 96%; gross margin severely hit by brass cost inflation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 18-20% reiterated.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 13.5-14% maintained; management says it will be met on a full-year basis, implying a recovery after Q2.
Q2 expected to carry some residual impact as project orders still at old prices; project price revisions to flow from Q3.
Gross margin expected to return to ~51% from Q3 if brass and gas prices hold; Q1 gross margin was ~46%.
FY27 wage cost add-on of INR 18.3 crore (INR 6.3 crore one-time arrears plus INR 12 crore for the year); FY27 staff cost guided at ~INR 300 crore.
FY27 capex outlay ~INR 43 crore, mainly Faucetware brownfield expansion (capacity expected from Q4 FY27), efficiency, digital and infrastructure.
FY27 brand-building and marketing budget ~INR 85 crore, which management says can be increased.
Management declined to guide FY28 margins; said it would revisit at year end. Long-term margin of 16% not committed to a timeline.
capex_capacity: Sanitaryware utilisation 61% in Q1 FY27 (one kiln run in April-May; second kiln started June); both plants running from June at ~80% of total capacity.
Faucetware utilisation 96% in Q1; management says it can go beyond 100% via in-house and outsourced supply until brownfield expansion comes in from Q4 FY27.
Greenfield sanitaryware project (earlier INR 130-150 crore, deferred) to be reviewed by year-end; would take ~18 months to build once decided.
Internalising higher-selling SKUs from Morbi outsourcing partners; incremental casting-line investment of INR 2-3 crore.
Long-term in-house/outsourced split about 50:50; Sanitaryware skewed more towards outsourcing recently due to bought-out parts.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increases (March and May 2026): ~12% in Sanitaryware, ~16% in Faucetware; management says absorbed well by the market.
Price hikes reflected mainly in retail; project contracts (43% of Q1 revenue vs 39% in Q4) to move to revised pricing from Q3.
Brass prices rose from INR 665 (Dec) to ~INR 880 (June) and ~INR 900 (July) per management; further hike possible if prices go to INR 950-1,000.
Product mix: premium 44%, mid 37%, entry 19%. Tier 1 and Tier 3 at 38% each, Tier 2 at 24%.
Management described growth as volume-driven and broad-based across retail and project, with Sanitaryware demand up from ~10% growth in prior quarters to 14%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 19.5% growth was volume vs price, and what was the Senator/Polipluz contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware: volume ~10%, price ~2%, mix ~2%. Faucetware: volume 18%, price 4%, mix 3%. Management would not split out Senator and Polipluz numbers, saying they are in build-up phase and FY27 targets are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-time wage settlement and what is the staff cost run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 6.3 crore arrears for Sept 2025-Mar 2026 booked in Q1, plus INR 3 crore for the current quarter. Full-year wage impact INR 18.3 crore. Staff cost expected ~INR 300 crore for FY27 excluding the one-off.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the margin drop, and how much is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 4.35 percentage point one-time impact: wage arrears 1.3%, under-absorption from single kiln 0.75% (INR 3.7 crore), accelerated project order closures 0.8% (INR 4 crore), and delayed retail price pass-through 1.5%. Ex-these items EBITDA would be ~14.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Morbi and SKU internalisation need capex, and how many flagship stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Internalisation needs only INR 2-3 crore of casting-line changes. Senator stores to rise from 35 to ~50 by year end, on track.

qa_highlights.question: Who leads Senator and Polipluz after Mr. Baliga's resignation?
qa_highlights.answer: The existing national head under the succession plan will lead them. Baliga stays until 30 September. Management says targets are unchanged and no execution impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Should the greenfield sanitaryware plant be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand improving (Sanitaryware growth 14% vs ~10% earlier). Review by year end; if approved the plant takes ~18 months. Some capacity remains available.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further price hikes and where does gross margin go?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin ~46% in Q1 (Faucetware hit hardest); expected ~51% from Q3 if brass and gas hold. Further hike to be evaluated if brass goes beyond INR 900-950.
